import os
import math
import numpy as np
import pychrono as chrono
import pychrono.robot as robot
from pychrono import irrlicht as chronoirr

# Create Chrono system
system = chrono.ChSystemNSC()
system.SetCollisionSystemType(chrono.ChCollisionSystem.Type_BULLET)
system.SetGravitationalAcceleration(chrono.ChVector3d(0, 0, -9.81))
chrono.ChCollisionModel.SetDefaultSuggestedEnvelope(0.0025)
chrono.ChCollisionModel.SetDefaultSuggestedMargin(0.0025)

# Create ground body with contact material and add it to the system
ground_mat = chrono.ChContactMaterialNSC()
ground = chrono.ChBodyEasyBox(20, 20, 1, 1000, True, True, ground_mat)
ground.SetPos(chrono.ChVector3d(0, 0, -0.5))  # Position the ground slightly below the origin
ground.SetFixed(True)  # Fix the ground in place
ground.GetVisualShape(0).SetTexture(chrono.GetChronoDataFile("textures/concrete.jpg"))
system.Add(ground)

# create a long box for rover to cross
box = chrono.ChBodyEasyBox(0.25, 5, 0.25, 1000, True, True, ground_mat)
box.SetPos(chrono.ChVector3d(0, 0, 0.0))
box.SetFixed(True)
box.GetVisualShape(0).SetTexture(chrono.GetChronoDataFile("textures/blue.png"))
system.Add(box)
# Create Curiosity rover and add it to the system
rover = robot.Curiosity(system)

# Create driver for rover
driver = robot.CuriosityDCMotorControl()
rover.SetDriver(driver)

# Initialize rover position and orientation
init_pos = chrono.ChVector3d(-5, 0.0, 0)
init_rot = chrono.ChQuaterniond(1, 0, 0, 0)
rover.Initialize(chrono.ChFramed(init_pos, init_rot))

# Create the Irrlicht visualization
vis = chronoirr.ChVisualSystemIrrlicht()
vis.AttachSystem(system)
vis.SetCameraVertical(chrono.CameraVerticalDir_Z)
vis.SetWindowSize(1280, 720)
vis.SetWindowTitle('Curiosity rover - Rigid terrain')
vis.Initialize()
vis.AddLogo(chrono.GetChronoDataFile('logo_pychrono_alpha.png'))
vis.AddSkyBox()
vis.AddCamera(chrono.ChVector3d(0, 3, 3), chrono.ChVector3d(0, 0, 0))
vis.AddTypicalLights()
vis.AddLightWithShadow(chrono.ChVector3d(1.5, -2.5, 5.5), chrono.ChVector3d(0, 0, 0), 3, 4, 10, 40, 512)

# Enable shadows (commented out to improve performance)
# vis.EnableShadows()

# Set the simulation time step
time_step = 1e-3

# Simulation loop
time = 0
while vis.Run():
    time += time_step

    # ask rover to move forward
    driver.SetSteering(0.0)

    # Update rover dynamics
    rover.Update()

    # Render the scene
    vis.BeginScene()
    vis.Render()
    vis.EndScene()

    # Advance simulation by one time step
    system.DoStepDynamics(time_step)

import os
import math
import numpy as np
import pychrono as chrono
import pychrono.robot as robot

import pychrono.sensor as sens  # Added import for sensor module

chrono.ChCollisionModel.SetDefaultSuggestedMargin(0.0025)

ground.GetVisualShape(0).SetTexture(chrono.GetChronoDataFile("textures/concrete.jpg"))
system.Add(ground)

box.SetPos(chrono.ChVector3d(0, 0, 0.0))

system.Add(box)

rover = robot.Curiosity(system)

driver = robot.CuriosityDCMotorControl()

# Initialize rover position and orientation

init_rot = chrono.ChQuaterniond(1, 0, 0, 0)

vis.AddTypicalLights()
vis.AddLightWithShadow(chrono.ChVector3d(1.5, -2.5, 5.5), chrono.ChVector3d(0, 0, 0), 3, 4, 10, 40, 512)

# Enable shadows (commented out to improve performance)

# Set the simulation time step

# Create sensor manager

# Add lidar sensor to the rover

    'update_rate': 10,

    'vertical_samples': 1,
    'field_of_view': math.pi / 2,
    'min_range': 0.1,
    'max_range': 100.0,
    'range_resolution': 0.01,
    'angle_resolution': math.pi / 180.0,
    'noise_stddev': 0.01,
    'filter_type': 'median'
}
lidar = sens.ChLidarSensor(rover.GetChassis(), **lidar_params)
rover.AddSensor(lidar)
manager.AddSensor(lidar)

# Simulation loop

while vis.Run():
    time += time_step

    # ask rover to move forward

    # Update rover dynamics
    rover.Update()

    # Update sensor manager
    manager.Update()

    # Render the scene
    vis.BeginScene()
    vis.Render()
    vis.EndScene()

    # Advance simulation by one time step
    system.DoStepDynamics(time_step)

import pychrono as pc
import pybullet as p
import pybullet_data

# Initialize PyChrono environment and core components
pc.init()

# Load the Bullet physics library and set up the simulation
physics_client = p.connect(p.GUI)
p.setGravity(0, 0, -9.81)
p.setAdditionalSearchPath(pybullet_data.getDataPath())

# Add the required physical systems and objects
# Fixed ground with collision properties
ground_id = p.loadURDF("plane.urdf", [0, 0, -1])

# Rover model with motor control driver for real-time steering inputs
rover_urdf_path = "path/to/your/rover.urdf"  # Replace with the path to your rover URDF file
rover_id = p.loadURDF(rover_urdf_path, [0, 0, 1])

# Set necessary default parameters
# Position the rover
p.resetBasePositionAndOrientation(rover_id, [0, 0, 1], [0, 0, 0, 1])

# Set motor control parameters (assuming you have a differential drive rover)
left_wheel_index = 0
right_wheel_index = 1
p.setJointMotorControl2(rover_id, left_wheel_index, p.VELOCITY_CONTROL, targetVelocity=0, force=100)
p.setJointMotorControl2(rover_id, right_wheel_index, p.VELOCITY_CONTROL, targetVelocity=0, force=100)

# Visualization using the Irrlicht visualization system with customizable camera settings, lighting, shadows, and additional visual elements like textures and logos
p.configureDebugVisualizer(p.COV_ENABLE_SHADOWS, 1)
p.configureDebugVisualizer(p.COV_ENABLE_GUI, 0)
p.setVisualizationSettings(p.VISUALIZATION_SETTINGS_ENABLE_GPU_VISUALIZATION)

# Set up camera
camera_distance = 5
camera_yaw = 45
camera_pitch = -30
p.resetDebugVisualizerCamera(camera_distance, camera_yaw, camera_pitch, [0, 0, 0])

# Simulation loop
while True:
    # Add your real-time steering inputs and other controls here
    # For example, you can use keyboard or joystick inputs to control the rover

    # Step the simulation
    p.stepSimulation()

    # Break the loop if the user closes the window
    if p.isConnected():
        break

# Disconnect from the physics server
p.disconnect()
